cultural.vision_reason: A narrow-strip hand-woven cloth sewn from alternating patterned strips, consistent with West African (including Toucouleur/Senegambian) strip-weaving traditions; nothing contradicts the attribution.

physical.title: cloth; textile
physical.summary: Cloth composed of 29 very narrow strips of two different widths, hand-woven from imported European thread, and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are of two patterns which are arranged alternately across the cloth. The first (of 15 narrower strips) is formed of blue weft squares that alternate with white squares of the same size; there is also a blue stripe along the centre of the warp. The second (of 14 wider strips) has a warp pattern that is formed from an arrangement of two blue threads and a green; at regular intervals supplementary bundles of weft threads in yellow and pale pink have been woven in, and both ends are terminated with six lines of red, green, blue and orange. The warp ends have been left loose and twisted and knotted to form a fringe.
